result.summary:
Corrected §11.2 and §11.4 of lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md per step-07b's single BLOCKER. Re-read step-07b's FAIL verdict in full plus the current §11.2 (lines 2175-2327) and §11.4 (lines 2375-2434) before editing.

§11.2 changes: (1) the section's opening 'Purpose' paragraph no longer states the mechanism's goal only in terms of '{shared, self()} mode' — it now states the goal as reusing whatever connection/mode the caller's test process is already using, naming both {shared, self()} (the common case) and :auto (the tenant_fixture_dispatch_test.exs case) up front. (2) The load-bearing 'Concrete mechanism' step 3 paragraph (previously: 'the caller's own {shared, self()} mode... is left completely alone') now states the property mode-agnostically: since this path issues no Sandbox.mode/2 call, whichever mode is ALREADY ambient at call time is left undisturbed — and explicitly walks through why tenant_fixture_dispatch_test.exs's own local `setup do Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) end` (line 60) means the ambient mode for that file is :auto by the time this path runs, per ExUnit's documented ordering (DataCase's injected setup runs before a module's own locally-declared setup). The DBConnection.Ownership.Manager owner-tracking sentence was extended to cover both the {shared, self()}-established-ownership case and the :auto-auto-checkout-established-ownership case (citing §9.3), rather than asserting only the former.

§11.4 changes: added a new bullet, positioned after the existing process-dictionary bullet, that names tenant_fixture_dispatch_test.exs directly, states the same ambient-mode fact as §11.2's correction, and explains that this file's read-correctness rests on §9.3's single-owner-under-:auto trace (fresh auto-checkout on first use, then reused as the same recorded owner for the rest of the test) rather than on the {shared, self()}-preserved property the rest of §11.4 relies on for the common case. The section's closing 'Conclusion' paragraph was extended to state both properties side by side (serialization argument for {shared, self()}; §9.3's single-owner trace for :auto) instead of citing only the first.

Also updated the file's top status line (originally just announcing '§11 ADDED') to record that §11.2/§11.4 were corrected in this same rework iteration and state the one-sentence nature of the fix, so a future reader opening the file cold sees the correction was made without needing to diff against step-07b.

Verification performed before finishing: (1) re-read both edited sections in full after editing to confirm the mode-agnostic property is stated as the PRIMARY claim, not appended as a caveat, and that tenant_fixture_dispatch_test.exs is named as a concrete instance in both sections, matching §11.2.1's own precedent for naming that file as the concrete instance of the template::replay override. (2) Grepped the file for fenced code blocks (```) after editing: same 10 blocks at the same pre-existing line clusters (~256/268, 668/677, 702/708, 1308/1314, 1459/1468), all inside §3/§9/§10 (superseded or quoted-for-evidence sections) as step-07b already confirmed — no new code block was introduced by this edit, and none exists inside §11. (3) Confirmed §11.1, §11.3, §11.5, §11.6, §11.7, §11.8 were not touched (only §11.2, §11.4, and the top-of-file status header were edited). (4) No OQ markers were added or resolved silently — this is a text restatement of an already-true conclusion (step-07b's own words: 'the conclusion... is still correct'), not a new finding requiring a new OQ.
